newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent bear island reversal still looms.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent bear island reversal still looms.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+IPE August Brent crude is expected to trade firmer on Monday and is likely to test resistance at around $18 a barrel.
+This is around the level of last week's bear island reversal which still looms gloomily over the market.
+Gas oil is also seen moving higher and the focus for the markets is around $160 a tonne.
IPE Brent crude oil futures are expected to test higher on Monday and traders and technical analysts see $17.98-$18 as an important focus for the markets.

August Brent closed 11 cents a barrel lower on Friday at $17.67 after reaching down as low as $17.48. July gas oil closed $1 a tonne down at $158.50. Traders expected Brent to open some 20 cents a barrel higher on Monday, and gas oil to open around $1.50 firmer.
Peter Sceats at CharTech-MCS said that a bear island reversal for Brent on the spot month continuation chart from last week was "the important short term pattern for the market at this time."
The reversal stems from a $17.98/$18.02 gap up on Tuesday, followed by a high to $18.32, and then a gap down from $18.02 to $17.98.
"While Brent is south of $18.02 the odds on further downside moves must stay shortened," Sceats said.
He was also negative about the market this week.
"If the Brent market rallies significantly in the coming week it won't be anything to do with the current price pattern."
But Tom James at Credit Lyonnais in Singapore said the market was initially likely to test up towards these levels on Monday.

"We are looking to open a bit firmer in London and the upside will probably be tested," he said, adding resistance would be encountered at $17.95-$18 a barrel - a layer of congestion from previous trades.

Gas oil, he said, was likely to look at the psychologically important level of $160 a tonne. "But below that, there is nothing much. It has destroyed all the trendlines recently - there may be a little light support a dollar below that."
